GTA 6 Should “Blaze A Trail” To More Expensive Games, Dev Says
items.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 is priced at $80 for its standard edition. Another voice has come forward to say they hope ot

content.v: Rockstar's GTA 6 is priced at $80 for its standard edition. Another voice has come forward to say they hope other teams follow suit and charge more for new games to help the industry at a time when developers are closing up shop, cancelling games, and laying off developers on a regular basis.
Martin Klima, the co-founder of Kingdom Come developer Warhorse, told PC Gamer that raising unit prices would "help a lot," but "everybody's scared to death" to do it.

"Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost," he said, adding that Rockstar and Take-Two are among the only companies who can "afford, or who can dare" to raise prices in this way.
He added that price increases for new games are "long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Ambrosia_05_3fee31.jpg?w=636

Take-Two was among the first big publishers to drive prices up from $60 to $70, kicking this off with NBA 2K21 in 2020. Numerous other publishers followed suit, and now $70 is the norm. Defending the price increase, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said production costs increased by 300%.

Former PlayStation executive Shawn Layden said in 2025 that the price of new games should have gone up with every new console generation for the past 20 years. That largely did not happen, and now the industry is worse off for it, he said.

“I think it’s because everyone’s afraid,” he told GI.biz . “No one wants to be the first one to raise the price, because you’re afraid to lose traffic. So what you do is you just end up eating into your operating income, your profit margin.”

“There were more sports cars in the parking lot in the PS1 era than there were in the PS4 era, because if you’re selling 20 million units at $60 for something that only cost you $10 million to make, that’s different than selling 20 million units at $60 for something that cost you $160 million to make.”
To help make up the difference, developers have hawked things like microtransactions, DLC, and battle passes . If more games go up in price, those trends will likely continue, too.
Before GTA 6's price was revealed, a Bank of America stock analyst said Take-Two should charge $80 to help spur other publishers to follow suit .
We already have $80 games, as Nintendo charges $80 for Mario Kart World, saying the game's ambition justifies the price tag .

Every game is priced differently, even within the same publisher, as Take-Two launched Mafia: The Old Country for $50– to great success . For its part, Nintendo's newly released F ire Emblem: Fortune's Weave costs $80 for its physical edition or $70 for its digital counterpart.

GTA 6, which releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, also has a $100 Ultimate Edition and a $400 collector's edition that does not include the game. Zelnick said earlier this year that Rockstar could have leveraged the monumental demand for GTA 6 to c harge a higher price to consumers , but chose not to.

In addition to the mountains of money Rockstar and Take-Two are due to make off GTA 6 game sales, the game is likely to eventually have some kind of new version of GTA Online, and that's no doubt going to print money .

items.title: GTA 6 Takes The Ridiculous World We Live In And Turns It Up To 11
items.summary: Video games are usually a few steps removed from reality, but with Grand Theft Auto 6 , developer Rockstar Gam

content.v: Video games are usually a few steps removed from reality, but with Grand Theft Auto 6 , developer Rockstar Games aims to reflect and amplify the current state of the world with an "over the top" experience. As seen in the trailers and gameplay previews so far, GTA 6 is a contemporary game about doing whatever it takes to make it to the top, and that pursuit of fame and glory is often bookended by shootouts, car chases, and explosions in its Bonnie and Clyde narrative.

"If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face," senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said to Love Magazine . "Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world."

Humphries also described the world of GTA 6 as "a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity," as the protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, are polar opposites. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern described Lucina as an ambitious go-getter who'll do anything to get the life she dreams of, while Jason is bound by life's circumstances. "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other," Gauvey-Kern said.

GTA 6 is also making some big changes to the franchise formula, as getting out of trouble won't be as easy as hiding in an alley and waiting for your wanted level to drop. Actions have consequences, and with the cops being much smarter and more persistent, players will have to be more cunning before they embark on a crime spree. The relationship between Jason and Lucia is also surprisingly more nuanced and deeper than you think, and it'll be a major part of the overall GTA 6 experience when the game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

With the wait almost over, the marketing machine for GTA 6 has begun to get into gear. Advertising has already taken over a Miami stadium , and the NBA's Miami Heat have announced they'll wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they face off against the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18. Rockstar Games also announced a $400 GTA 6 Collector's Edition last week; while it doesn't include the game, it does include various trinkets typically associated with users of the devil's dandruff.

items.title: I added October-appropriate zombies to Grand Theft Auto 5

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

There is no more room in hell—the dead are at the beach. Grand Theft Auto 5, already burdened and bedraggled by the parade of mods I have inflicted on it, must now contend with a new disorder: revenants from beyond the veil.

I have installed ZombieInfection , which adds zombie and, indeed, infection. In any given populated space, you will look about yourself to notice that some of Los Santos' denizens are more bloody and shambling than usual. This is because they have been rejected by the grave.

Whenever these undead pedestrians brush up against other city-dwellers, the latter converts instantly to the horde. Before long, what began as just two or three bloodied weirdos becomes a city-threatening catastrophe, which is both horrifying and a good way of demonstrating the power of exponential growth.

Fortunately, zombies are just as prone to the impact of tornadoes, cars, fire, and so on as anyone else. They're also rather slow. More often than not, they get taken out by one of Los Santos' countless ambient threats before they can do any real damage. A lesson for mayors everywhere.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2NyD6cHwCabsi97uESHcG-1920-80.gif

Shockingly, the curse of the undeath is so strong that it can somehow break my own aura of immortality. Franklin—you may have noticed from previous articles, where he does things like surviving tornadoes and being used as a ramp by cars—is invincible in my GTA 5 install. But let a zombie brush up against him for long enough and he will succumb to the afterworld like any other mortal. It's very scary. Happy Halloween.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass Loses These 9 Games In October
items.summary: The start of the month usually brings several new Xbox Game Pass titles for subscribers, along with confirmati

others.title: A surprisingly in-depth dressmaking simulator has the cosy gamers in a chokehold

content.v: The start of the month usually brings several new Xbox Game Pass titles for subscribers, along with confirmation of which games will leave the subscription service in the coming days. This month, at least nine games will be leaving, including one of the best games of 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

Other big departures this month include A Plague Tale: Requiem and-- inconveniently for horror fans during the spookiest month of the year--the Dead by Daylight spin-off The Casting of Frank Stone . Evil West is another great game you only have a few days left to play, with a solid 7/10 experience full of monster-slaying energy.
Pacific Drive was another one of our favorites when it was released a few years back, as this eerie roguelite driving game combined a tense atmosphere with themes of mystery and survival.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/original/1849/18498836/4481170-expedition33.jpg?w=636
Leaving Xbox Game Pass on October 15
As a reminder, you can save 20% on these games if you decide to buy them before they leave Game Pass.
September was a pretty big month for Game Pass removals, with a total of 18 games packing their bags. The list included some big titles, like The Witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077, Sifu, and Frostpunk 2.

items.title: MTG’s Hobbit Cards Are the Closest Thing to Owning Rare Tolkien Memorabilia, and Perfect for Collectors
items.summary: Here's why Magic: The Gathering’s small-ish Hobbit set somehow surpasses the massive Lord of the Rings crossov

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/02/img-2807-1790937934930.JPG

For the second time, and likely the last, Magic: The Gathering has taken players back to Middle-Earth with its The Hobbit set (its fifth of the year, if you can believe it), and it’s been pretty great.

That’s perhaps to be expected since the original book laid out a lot of what we consider fantasy tropes. Dragons, goblins, dwarves, and more are represented here in a smaller set than the Lord of the Rings one, all of which have gone on to inspire Magic cards in their own right.

Still, given how tricky it can be to get some products, there’s a good chance that finding Hobbit items can feel like searching for the Arkenstone in Smaug’s treasure hoard. And yet, it feels like, in a way, that’s kind of the point.
Tolkien Collectors Will Love The Hobbit Set
J.R.R. Tolkien’s influence on the world of fantasy cannot be overstated, and there’s a reason that so many early editions of his works have fetched colossal sums of money.
As an example, back in 2025, a fully signed Lord of the Rings first-edition set sold for around £287,700 (or $337,000). That marks the high point of spending, but it’s not an outlier by any stretch.
An unsigned first edition of the book also sold in 2025 for $250,000, while a collection of manuscripts from the author that includes notes written in Elvish has sold for over $200,000, too.

Naturally, memorabilia sells big, too, notably from Peter Jackson’s iconic movies. Props, costumes, and limited-edition art prints fetch piles of gold to make a covetous dragon blush, and that includes pieces from The Hobbit movies, too.
Of course, those figures are colossal compared to the price of even the most expensive cards in The Hobbit set , but there’s crossover there, too.

Whereas the Lord of the Rings set offered full art cards with a slick border treatment that highlighted the series’ characters across heroes and villains, The Hobbit leans into the series’ literary origins with book cover-inspired designs that carry a “well-read” look that makes them feel unique amongst Magic’s wide-ranging treatment offerings.

This writer was lucky enough to pack Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane and Smaug, Wicked Worm in the treatment, and they’ve almost instantly become two of my favorite Magic cards I own. There’s just something about the way they look textured that makes them feel like the latest in a long line of Tolkien memorabilia.
In fact, I’d go so far as to say that these are my favorite treatments we’ve received in years - and an ideal inclusion for any serious collector.
That doesn’t make it any easier to find the cards, mind…

items.title: The upcoming sim about making games is so deep your in-game game can even get cyberleeked
items.summary: Let's Build a Dungeon isn't just about making a game, but all the stuff you have to deal with while making a g

content.v: Of all the games on the horizon, the one I may be most looking forward to Let's Build a Dungeon . It's a sim from Springloaded, makers of Let's Build a Zoo and the upcoming RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks , and the premise is one we've all mulled at one point or another: what if I could make my own videogame?

And in Let's Build a Dungeon, you can. Dig dungeons, populate them with monsters and traps and loot, design quests, and watch simulated players play your game. You'll even be able to let real players play the game you make.

But there's also the simulation surrounding the game you're building. The development studio you've founded. The devs you hire. You'll have to deal with investors, finances, the public, the press (like me!), crunch, gaming conventions, hackers, and even text messages from your mom.

There's a lot going on in this sim. Like, a lot , a lot. During a recent preview and interview with Springloaded founder and Let's Build a Dungeon lead developer James Barnard , here's what leapt out at me as being the most a lot among the lot.
"We have, like, 700 [fictional] games or something, and the list keeps on getting longer."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/UBDi92zSvpGyqKjDn4pfGP-1920-80.jpg
Let's Build a Dungeon lead developer and Springloaded founder

Let's Build a Dungeon simulates Steam's backend and sites like SteamSpy where you can see your game alongside the competition. Lots of competition: Springloaded has invented hundreds of fictional (and unplayable, sadly) games to populate your reality.
"We have all these games, which obviously our concept artist, poor guy, he spent his his whole life drawing these things."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/b9pNeZgsm2zD2ZU9XNWJrC-1920-80.jpg
And look, there's even an advert for a gaming show. A computer gaming show. That's a great idea for an event! Someone should do that for real.

"You can see sort of how your game is doing with the wishlists and things like that. The objective is to get into events, and if you do, you get massive number of impressions. So we really use the impressions, click through rate, conversions, wishlists , and all of that stuff feeds into the chart."

"When you go from CGA to VGA, you have to upgrade some of your computers, and then the size of everything expands and becomes bigger, so suddenly you need more hard drive space because all your assets are now high resolution."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6GcF3WpKQkNsKY3XgcyLvC-1920-80.jpg

The fictional game you're making in Let's Build a Dungeon runs on fictional hardware, and as your game gets bigger, it takes up more space. Time is passing, too, meaning there are advances in PC hardware as well as your game's required specs, and that's reflected in the sim.
" We drew every single component of every computer, so there's about 150 components that we drew from, and it goes through the history of computing."
You won't just see a difference, you'll hear one. The soundtrack of the game will change based on the audio card your simulated computer is using.
Buying plane tickets and booking hotels for your devs to attend game showcases is a "ridiculous minigame" that even simulates layovers
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6xrmEDayb3rTiZTcvWLSsC-1920-80.jpg

"Once [your employees] head off to the [showcase], you get to pick who's going to go to the event, and then they aren't working, so they won't appear in your design board. If I send these two people to an event, they're going to disappear for three days and and, you know, fuck up my schedule.

"The flights kind of curve up in price as you get closer to the day, but then sometimes there'll be a bargain right at the end if they've got too many seats to sell, and the same for the hotel. So if you wait till the last minute, you sort of take this risk of: Am I going to spend too much?

"We calculate where you started your company and where the event is. We actually calculate the distance and how long it takes and we do the stopovers in the right cities , so where your office is, is gonna impact you. So if you get EGX Rezzed, it's just down the road for you, if you pick London."
Remember Cyberleek? That could happen to you
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PpuAiEquGmb7QxjNvFMPG9-1920-80.jpg

"This is some super nerd who's basically hacked your computer. Oh no, he's been following your investors' flights around the world, and he's decided that you are making an MMO, and he's looked at your financials and the other guy's financials, and then he holds you to ransom.
" He's either going to leak the game, or he's or he's going to convince you to put him in the game . There's lots of different outcomes."
Your mum sends you pie recipes and cat videos
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rMw8kQEVkxt7jehojfGMfN-1920-80.jpg
"Your mum calls you. Have you eaten? And then she tries to make you eat different food, and gives you desktop screenshots and things for rewards.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8DZXKNLuZjzrXmqpVHvZQN-1920-80.jpg
"And this conversation, for example, you can get a song, you can get like different desktop images to cheer you up because she wants you to be encouraged in your daily life.

"One of the other things she gives you is a pie, and then she sends you the recipe for the pie, and then you get inspired, and you add a the ability for your designers to come up with a pie recipe, and then you get a pie that you can put in the game , and the players can eat, and you can adjust all that kind of stuff."

By the way, if all of this game dev studio simulation stuff isn't your thing and you just want to use Let's Build a Dungeon to design your own game, you can do that too! There's a campaign mode, build mode, creative mode, or just play the games created by other players.
Let's Build a Dungeon is coming to early access in February . There's a demo you can try in the meantime.
